message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills and modern scares you might enjoy for a Friday‑night movie marathon:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** (1980) | A psychological thriller set in an isolated hotel, featuring Jack Nicholson’s iconic descent into madness. |
| 2 | **Get Out** (2017) | A smart social satire wrapped in a horror package; it blends dread with sharp commentary on race. |
| 3 | **Hereditary** (2018) | A slow‑burn family drama that turns into a nightmare; the atmosphere is oppressive and the ending is unforgettable. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Suspense built around silence—every footstep could mean death. Great for a tense, edge‑of‑your‑seat experience. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** (2019) | A daylight horror that subverts expectations; the bright Swedish setting makes the gore even more jarring. |
| 6 | **It Follows** (2014) | An inventive premise where a curse is transmitted through sexual contact; the creeping dread is relentless. |
| 7 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | A well‑crafted paranormal investigation that balances jump‑scares with genuine tension. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** (2014) | A psychological horror about grief and motherhood; the monster is as much metaphorical as literal. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** (1977) | If you’re up for something surreal, Dario Argento’s color‑splashed ballet of terror will leave you unsettled. |
|10 | **The Witch** (2015) | A period piece that slowly builds dread through atmosphere and unsettling dialogue. |

Feel free to pick one or two from each era for variety, or stick to a single theme if you want a cohesive binge. Happy watching!
